ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The picture shows a central square with one triangle attached to each side of the square, forming a four-point star. The bases of the four triangles coincide with the sides of the square, so those base segments are internal and not on the outside boundary. The outside boundary of the star is made from the two exposed sides of each attached triangle. Reasoning: The perimeter of the square is 36 cm, so each side of the square is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm. Each triangle has all sides equally long, so each exposed side of every triangle is also 9 cm. There are 4 triangles, and each contributes 2 exposed outer sides, for 4 × 2 = 8 boundary sides. Therefore, the star perimeter is 8 × 9 = 72 cm.

method.method_draft: Treat the star as a union of one square and four equilateral triangles. From the text, the square side is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm. Each triangle has perimeter 3 × 9 = 27 cm, so four triangles have total perimeter 108 cm, and the square has perimeter 36 cm. If these perimeters are added, the four shared edges between the square and triangles are counted twice but are not on the outside; their total length is 4 × 9 = 36 cm, so subtract 2 × 36 = 72 cm. Thus the outside perimeter is 36 + 108 − 72 = 72 cm.
